²⁶ They are gone like swift ships, like an eagle diving on its prey. ²⁷ If I say, "I will put my grief aside, I will set down my sorrow and find some comfort" — ²⁸ I am terrified by all my suffering, for I know you will not clear me of guilt. ²⁹ If I am already condemned, why should I struggle for nothing? ³⁰ Even if I scrubbed myself with snow and cleansed my hands with lye, ³¹ you would plunge me into a pit, and my own clothes would recoil from me.

³² He is not a man like me, that I could answer him, that we could stand together before a court. ³³ There is no one to mediate between us, no one who could lay his hand on us both. ³⁴ Let him take his rod away from me, let his terror no longer overwhelm me — ³⁵ then I would speak without fear, for that is not how I am in myself.

[Chapter 10] ¹ My soul is sick of life. I will pour out my complaint freely; I will speak from the bitterness of my soul. ² I will say to God, "Do not condemn me — show me why you are contending with me. ³ Does it please you to oppress me, to despise the work of your own hands, while you smile on the schemes of the wicked? ⁴ Do you see as a mortal sees? Do you look on things the way humans do? ⁵ Are your days like the days of a man, your years like a man's years,

⁶ that you must search out my sin and seek out my wrongdoing? ⁷ You know that I am not guilty, and no one can rescue me from your hand. ⁸ Your own hands shaped me and made me — and now you turn and destroy me? ⁹ Remember that you formed me like clay. Will you return me to dust? ¹⁰ Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?

¹¹ You clothed me with skin and flesh, you knit me together with bones and sinews. ¹² You gave me life and showed me steadfast love, and your care has preserved my spirit. ¹³ Yet these things you hid in your heart — I know this was your purpose all along. ¹⁴ If I sinned, you would be watching, and you would not let my guilt go unpunished. ¹⁵ If I am wicked, then woe to me; and even if I am righteous, I dare not lift my head — I am so filled with shame, soaked in my own misery.

¹⁶ And if I hold my head up, you hunt me like a fierce lion, and turn your power against me once more. ¹⁷ You bring fresh witnesses against me, and your anger toward me grows — blow after blow, wave after wave of assault. ¹⁸ Then why did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before any eye had seen me, ¹⁹ that I had been carried from the womb to the grave, as though I had never existed. ²⁰ The few days of my life are almost spent — leave me alone, let me have a little comfort

²¹ before I go to the place I will never return from — the land of darkness and the shadow of death, ²² a land as dark as the darkness itself, where the shadow of death covers all, where there is no order, and where the light is as dark as night.

[Chapter 11] ¹ Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said: ² "Should all these words go unanswered? Should a man who talks so much be proved right? ³ Should your empty words silence everyone? Should you mock, and no one call you out? ⁴ You claim your beliefs are sound, that you are pure in God's eyes. ⁵ But if only God would speak, if only he would open his lips against you,

⁶ and tell you the secrets of wisdom — for true wisdom has two sides. Know this: God is not even holding you fully accountable for all your wrongdoing. ⁷ Can you fathom the depths of God? Can you probe the limits of the Almighty? ⁸ They are higher than the heavens — what can you do? Deeper than the grave — what can you know? ⁹ Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea. ¹⁰ If he passes through and puts someone in prison, or calls a court to order, who can stop him?

¹¹ For he knows who is hollow — when he sees wickedness, does he not take note of it? ¹² An empty-headed person will no more become wise than a wild donkey's colt can be born human. ¹³ But if you set your heart right, and stretch out your hands to him — ¹⁴ if you put away the sin that is in your hands, and let no wrong dwell in your tent, ¹⁵ then you will be able to lift your face without shame; you will stand firm and without fear.

¹⁶ You will forget your misery; you will remember it only as water that has flowed past. ¹⁷ Your life will be brighter than noon; even the darkness will be like morning. ¹⁸ You will feel secure, because there is hope; you will look around and rest in safety. ¹⁹ You will lie down with no one to make you afraid, and many will come seeking your favor. ²⁰ But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and their escape will be cut off, and their hope will be nothing but their last breath."

[Chapter 12] ¹ Then Job answered and said: ² "No doubt you are the people who matter, and wisdom will die with you. ³ But I have a mind as well as you — I am no less than you. Who does not know these things? ⁴ I have become a laughingstock to my friends — I, who called on God and he answered me, a just and blameless man who has become a laughingstock. ⁵ The one who is comfortable has contempt for misfortune — it is the fate of those whose feet are slipping.

⁶ The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke God live securely — those whom God has given everything they want. ⁷ But ask the animals, and they will teach you; ask the birds of the sky, and they will tell you; ⁸ ask the earth, and it will teach you; let the fish of the sea explain it to you. ⁹ Which of all these does not know that the hand of the Lord has done this? ¹⁰ In his hand is the life of every living creature, and the breath of all mankind.

¹¹ Does the ear not test words, just as the tongue tastes food? ¹² Wisdom belongs to the aged, and understanding to those who have lived long. ¹³ But with God are wisdom and power; he has both counsel and understanding. ¹⁴ What he tears down cannot be rebuilt; whoever he shuts in cannot get out. ¹⁵ If he holds back the waters, they dry up; if he unleashes them, they overwhelm the land.

¹⁶ With him are strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver both belong to him. ¹⁷ He leads counselors away stripped bare, and makes fools of judges. ¹⁸ He breaks off the chains that kings put on others, and ties a loincloth around their own waists. ¹⁹ He leads priests away stripped bare, and overthrows those who have stood firm for ages. ²⁰ He silences the lips of trusted advisors, and takes away the discernment of the elders.

²¹ He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong. ²² He uncovers deep things from the darkness and brings into the light the shadow of death. ²³ He makes nations great, then destroys them; he enlarges nations, then drives them away. ²⁴ He strips the understanding away from the leaders of the nations and makes them wander in a trackless waste. ²⁵ They grope in the dark without light, and he makes them stagger like drunkards.

[Chapter 13] ¹ All of this my eye has seen; my ear has heard and understood it. ² What you know, I know also — I am not less than you. ³ But I want to speak to the Almighty; I want to argue my case before God. ⁴ You, however, are smearing things with lies — you are worthless doctors, all of you. ⁵ If only you would keep silent — that would be your wisdom.

⁶ Hear now my argument; listen to the case I will make with my lips. ⁷ Will you speak falsely on God's behalf? Will you speak deceitfully for him? ⁸ Will you show him partiality? Will you make his case for him? ⁹ Will it go well when he examines you? Can you deceive him as one deceives a man? ¹⁰ He will surely rebuke you if you secretly show partiality.

¹¹ Will not his majesty strike terror into you? Will not the dread of him fall upon you? ¹² Your wise sayings are proverbs of ash; your defenses are defenses of clay. ¹³ Keep silent before me — let me speak, and let whatever comes, come. ¹⁴ Why should I put myself at risk and take my life into my own hands? ¹⁵ Even if he kills me, I will hope in him — I will still defend my ways to his face.

¹⁶ This very thing will be my salvation — that a godless person cannot come before him. ¹⁷ Listen carefully to my words; let my declaration ring in your ears. ¹⁸ I have set out my case — I know that I will be vindicated. ¹⁹ Who would bring charges against me? If anyone can, I will fall silent and die. ²⁰ Only grant me two things, O God, and then I will not hide myself from you:

²¹ withdraw your hand far from me, and let your terror no longer dismay me. ²² Then call out, and I will answer — or let me speak first, and you reply. ²³ How many wrongs and sins have I committed? Show me my offense; tell me my sin. ²⁴ Why do you hide your face and treat me as your enemy?

²⁶ For you write bitter things against me, and force me to inherit the sins of my youth. ²⁷ You put my feet in stocks; you stand watch over all my paths; you set a limit on the soles of my feet. ²⁸ And I, like a rotten thing, am wasting away — like a garment that moths have eaten.

[Chapter 14] ¹ A person born of woman has few days and much trouble. ² They come up like a flower, then wither; they flee like a shadow and do not last. ³ Do you really open your eyes on such a person? Do you really bring me into judgment with you? ⁴ Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one. ⁵ A person's days are determined; you know the number of their months; you have set limits they cannot go beyond.

⁶ Look away from them and let them rest, until — like a hired worker — they have completed their day. ⁷ There is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its new shoots will keep coming. ⁸ Though its root grows old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil, ⁹ at the scent of water it will bud again and put out branches like a young plant. ¹⁰ But a person dies and lies still; they breathe their last, and then where are they?

¹¹ As water vanishes from a lake, and a river drains away and dries up, ¹² so a person lies down and does not rise again; until the heavens are no more, they will not awake, and they will not be roused from their sleep. ¹³ Oh, that you would hide me in the grave, that you would conceal me until your anger has passed, and set a time for me and then remember me! ¹⁴ If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard labor I would wait, hoping for my release.

¹⁶ For now you count my every step; you watch over my sin. ¹⁷ My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and you sew up my guilt. ¹⁸ Yet as a mountain crumbles away and falls, and as a rock shifts from its place, ¹⁹ as water wears away stones, as floods sweep away the topsoil of the ground — so you destroy a person's hope. ²⁰ You overpower them once and for all, and they are gone; you change their appearance and send them away.

²¹ Their children come to honor, and they do not know it; their children are brought low, and they do not see it. ²² Only this do they feel: their own body's pain; only this do they mourn: themselves.

[Chapter 15] ¹ Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said: ² "Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge and fill himself up with the east wind? ³ Should he argue with useless talk, with words that do no good? ⁴ But you are undermining the fear of God and hindering devotion before him. ⁵ Your own guilt teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.

⁶ Your own mouth condemns you, not I — your own lips testify against you. ⁷ Were you the first person ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills? ⁸ Were you listening in on God's council? Do you have a monopoly on wisdom? ⁹ What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not understand? ¹⁰ Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us — men older even than your father.

¹¹ Are God's consolations not enough for you? Is the word spoken gently to you not sufficient? ¹² Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash, ¹³ so that you turn your spirit against God and let such words pour from your mouth? ¹⁴ What is a mortal, that they should be clean? What is one born of woman, that they should be righteous? ¹⁵ If God puts no trust even in his holy ones, and even the heavens are not pure in his sight,

¹⁶ how much more corrupt and depraved is a person who drinks in evil like water! ¹⁷ I will show you — listen to me — and I will tell you what I have seen; ¹⁸ what wise men have declared without hiding, passed down from their fathers, ¹⁹ to whom the land was given while no stranger moved among them. ²⁰ The wicked are in torment all their days, and the years that have been stored up for the ruthless are few.

²¹ Terrifying sounds fill their ears; in the midst of peace, the destroyer comes upon them. ²² They do not believe they will return from darkness, and they are destined for the sword. ²³ They wander about, asking, "Where can I find bread?" — knowing that a day of darkness is ready at hand. ²⁴ Distress and anguish terrify them; they overpower them, like a king ready for battle.

²⁵ Because they have stretched out their hand against God and defied the Almighty, ²⁶ charging at him with a stiff neck, with the thick bosses of their shields — ²⁷ because they covered their face with fat and made their waist thick with flesh, ²⁸ they live in desolate cities, in houses that no one else inhabits, houses crumbling into ruins. ²⁹ They will no longer be rich; their wealth will not endure, and their possessions will not spread over the earth. ³⁰ They will not escape the darkness; flames will wither their shoots, and they will depart by the breath of God's mouth.

³¹ Let them not trust in emptiness and deceive themselves — emptiness will be their reward. ³² Their branch will wither before its time, and their shoots will not be green. ³³ They will be like a vine that shakes off its unripe grapes, like an olive tree casting off its blossoms. ³⁴ For the company of the godless will produce nothing, and fire will consume the tents of those who take bribes. ³⁵ They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb brings forth deception."

[Chapter 16] ¹ Then Job answered and said: ² "I have heard all of this before. You are miserable comforters, every one of you. ³ Will your windy words never end? What is driving you to keep answering? ⁴ I could speak just as you do — if you were in my place, I could heap words together against you and shake my head at you. ⁵ I could strengthen you with my mouth and move my lips to ease your pain.

⁶ But when I speak, my pain is not relieved; and when I hold back, it does not leave me. ⁷ Surely he has worn me out now; he has made my whole community desolate. ⁸ He has shriveled me up — and this is evidence against me; my wasting body rises up and testifies to my face. ⁹ He tears me apart in his anger and hates me; he gnashes his teeth at me; my enemy pierces me with his eyes. ¹⁰ People gape at me with open mouths; they strike my cheek with contempt; they mass together against me.

¹¹ God has handed me over to the ungodly and thrown me into the hands of the wicked. ¹² I was living in peace, but he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and smashed me to pieces, then set me up as his target. ¹³ His archers surround me; he pierces my kidneys without mercy and pours out my bile on the ground. ¹⁴ He breaks through me, breach after breach; he charges at me like a warrior. ¹⁵ I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and buried my brow in the dust.

¹⁶ My face is red from weeping, and dark shadows ring my eyes — ¹⁷ though there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is sincere. ¹⁸ O earth, do not cover my blood; let my cry find no resting place. ¹⁹ Even now, my witness is in heaven; my advocate is on high. ²⁰ My friends scorn me, but my eyes pour out tears to God.
²¹ Oh, that someone would plead with God on behalf of a person, as one pleads for a friend! ²² For only a few years will pass before I go down the path from which I will not return.

[Chapter 17] ¹ My spirit is broken; my days are snuffed out; the grave is waiting for me. ² I am surrounded by mockers — my eyes rest on their hostility. ³ Put up a pledge for me with yourself — who else is there to put up security for me? ⁴ For you have closed their minds to understanding; therefore you will not let them triumph.

⁶ He has made me a byword among the people; I have become someone people spit in the face of. ⁷ My eye has grown dim with grief, and all my limbs are like a shadow. ⁸ Upright people are appalled at this; the innocent are stirred up against the godless. ⁹ But the righteous hold to their path, and those with clean hands grow stronger.

¹¹ My days are past; my plans are torn apart, the very desires of my heart. ¹² They turn night into day, saying the light is near when darkness is all around me. ¹³ If my only hope is to go to the grave, if I have made my bed in the darkness, ¹⁴ if I have said to the pit, "You are my father," and to the worm, "You are my mother" and "my sister" — ¹⁵ where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
¹⁶ Will hope go down with me to the gates of death? Will we descend together into the dust?

[Chapter 18] ¹ Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said: ² "How long before you stop making speeches? Think carefully, and then we will speak. ³ Why do you treat us as animals — as stupid in your eyes? ⁴ You who tear yourself apart in your anger — shall the earth be abandoned for your sake? Shall rocks be moved from their place?

⁶ The light in his tent will grow dark, and the lamp beside him will be snuffed out. ⁷ His strong stride will falter, and his own schemes will bring him down. ⁸ His own feet throw him into a net; he walks right into the trap. ⁹ A snare catches him by the heel and holds him fast. ¹⁰ A noose is hidden in the ground for him, a trap lies across his path.

¹¹ Terrors beset him on every side and chase him at every step. ¹² Calamity is hungry for him, and disaster stands ready at his side. ¹³ Disease devours his skin; death's firstborn eats away his limbs. ¹⁴ He is torn from the security he trusted in and marched off to the king of terrors.
